result_text:
Template literals are now blanked during unit comparison, the same way `"..."` and `'...'` literals already are. Two JavaScript or TypeScript functions that differ only inside a backtick literal are reported as one duplicated unit. The full `codeanalyzer` test suite passes (332 run, 0 failures, 3 skipped).

**What changed**

- `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/lang/js/JavaScriptHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java`: overrides `extraCleanContent` to replace each `` `...` `` literal with `` `` `` before the existing quote rules run. Line breaks inside a multi-line literal are kept, because unit line numbers are mapped by line index. TypeScript inherits this extractor, so it gets the same behaviour.
- `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/lang/js/JavaScriptHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest.java`: two tests. One checks that `` `Hello alpha ${name}` `` and `` `Hello beta ${name}` `` give one duplicate with two blocks. The other checks that a difference outside the literal (`+ name`) keeps the units apart.

**Choices I made**

- I scoped the change to the JavaScript extractor instead of the shared C-style code. Go raw strings and Kotlin/Scala backtick identifiers also use backticks, and blanking them globally would have changed those languages too.
- The duplicate check ignores a second unit from the same file path, so the tests put each function in its own file.

I did not run `mvn install`, so the `reports` and `codeexplorer` modules will only show the new behaviour after `codeanalyzer` is reinstalled. Nothing is committed.
